intro.title: rem and em
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with text elements to understand and apply the CSS units 'rem' and 'em'. You will learn how 'rem' is based on the root element's font size and 'em' is relative to its parent element's font size. The core concept involves using these relative units to create scalable and maintainable designs. You will work with CSS properties like font-size, padding, and margin. By the end, you'll be able to control spacing and sizing in a flexible way that adapts to different screen sizes and user preferences.
intro.usecase: The rem and em units are essential for building scalable and accessible user interfaces in real-world web applications. For example, in a responsive dashboard, developers use rem to set a consistent base font size for the entire layout, ensuring that all elements scale proportionally when a user adjusts their browser's default font settings. Within a complex navigation menu or a modal component, em units are used to size padding, margins, and font sizes relative to their parent container, allowing nested elements like buttons or icons to adapt seamlessly when the menu's font size changes. This approach is critical in design systems and component libraries, where maintaining visual harmony and accessibility across different screen sizes and user preferences is a key requirement for professional front-end development.
